texts.facts: Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197830268/ 1 Compensation case regarding grievous injury to Suraj Kumar AWARD 1. In this case, a detailed accident report was filed by police in terms of provisions of Motor Vehicle Act and same is treated as Claim Petition in view of the provisions contained in such Act. 2. Brief facts of the case are that on 31.05.2018, at about 02.00 PM, at injured was coming from his office(Faridabad) on office bus when bus reached Sarita Vihar bus stand around 3 pm and injured got down and crossing the service road to take a bus for Okhla, suddenly motorcycle bearing registration no. DL-3S-BN-6155 came from wrong side without giving any horn in very speed and neglecting manner hit the injured and he sustained grievous injuries. 3. He was taken to AIIMS Trauma Center where he was given emergency treatment and MLC bearing no. 500100198/18 dated 31.05.2018 was prepared by the doctors of the concerned hospital. As per MLC, petitioner suffered grievous injury. 4. The police after investigation, in FIR No. 142/18 filed charge sheet against respondent no.2 under Section 279/338 IPC & 146/196 & 115/190(2), 50/177 MV Act was also filed by the investigation officer. 5. In response to DAR, Driver & Owner appeared initially. But as per record, they did not file any reply and stopped participating in the MACT No. 147/2019 Suraj Kumar v. Arvind Kumar Page No. 2/18 BK proceedings. 6. In this case, as per material and DAR filed, the offending vehicle was without required insurance cover. OPP. 3) Relief. 8. Petitioner /injured Suraj Kumar entered the witness box as PW1 and filed his evidence by way of affidavit as Ex.PW1/1. He relied upon his MLC as Ex.PW1/A, copy of discharge summary issued from JPNA Trauma Center as Ex. PW-1/B, original medical store bills as Ex. PW- 1/B/A (colly), attested copy of DAR as Ex. PW-1/C, copy of PAN Card as Ex. PW-1/D and Aadhar card as Ex. PW-1/E, copy of 12th class educational certificate is Mark-A. Suraj Kumar vs Santosh Kumar Singh on 3 August, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197830268/ 2 9. Respondent no.1 and 2 did not cross-examine such witness. 10. No other evidence was led on behalf of petitioner, thereafter, PE was closed. 11. No evidence was led on behalf of respondents. The factors noted above are sufficient to conclude that preponderance of probability is made out showing negligence of respondent No. 1 in causing the accident. 16. In the present case, police after investigation had filed charge-sheet against respondent no.1 under section 279/338 of IPC which is also suggestive of negligence of respondent in causing the accident. The IO has filed Detailed Accident Report before this Tribunal. 17. Further, in his evidence by way of affidavit, PW-1 deposed that on 31.05.2018, at about 2 pm, he was coming from his office at Faridabad on office bus. Bus reached at Sarita Vihar bus stand at around 3 pm and injured got down from bus and while crossing road to take a bus for Okhla, suddenly the offending vehicle in question, motorcycle bearing no. DL-3S-BN-6155 was coming from wrong side without giving any horn at a very high speed and in negligent manner hit the injured/PW-1. As a result of which, PW-1 fell down and sustained injuries. He was removed to AIIMS Trauma Center, where his MACT No. 147/2019 Suraj Kumar v. Arvind Kumar Page No. 4/18 BK MLC Ex. PW-1/A was prepared and he was discharged on next day vide Ex. PW-1/B. He sustained grievous injuries on right leg and other parts of his bodies. PW-1 was not cross-examined by the respondents. On perusal of record, in this case, it may be noted that injured/petitioner while appearing into witness box as PW-1 made statement and narrated the Suraj Kumar vs Santosh Kumar Singh on 3 August, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197830268/ 3 mode and manner of the accident. He deposed that accident occurred due to the negligent driving of respondent no.-1, Arvind Kumar.
texts.arguments: In National Insurance Co. Vs. Pushpa Rana 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, it was laid down that completion of investigation and filing of chargesheet u/s 279/304A IPC are sufficient proof of negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle. 20. At this stage, before proceeding further, by rely upon the judgments of C.K. Subramania Iyer v. T. Kunhikuttan Nair, R.D. Hattangadi v. Pest Control (India) (P) Ltd. and Baker v. Willoughby which are referred and relied in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 Supreme Court cases 343 decided by Hon'ble SC, it can be noted that the provision of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ("the Act", for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident. The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury. 21. Further it can be noted that the heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following: Pecuniary damages (Special damages) (i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalisation, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure. (ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising: (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment; (b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability. Non-pecuniary damages (General damages) Suraj Kumar vs Santosh Kumar Singh on 3 August, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197830268/ 4 (v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage). (vi) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity). 21.1. 21.6. It was observed by Hon'ble Supreme Court in such case of Raj Kumar (supra) that what usually poses some difficulty is the assessment of the loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability--Item (ii) (a). 21.7. Disability refers to any restriction or lack of ability to perform an activity in the manner considered normal for a human being. 33. At this stage, it is relevant to the refer to the judgment of A. V. Padma & Ors. Vs., R. Venugopal & Ors. (2012) 3 Supreme Court Cases 378: " ......In the case of Susamma Thomas (supra), this Court issued certain guidelines in order to "safeguard the feed from being frittered away by the beneficiaries due to ignorance, illiteracy and susceptibility to exploitation". Moreover, in the case of Suraj Kumar vs Santosh Kumar Singh on 3 August, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197830268/ 10 literate persons, the Tribunal may resort to the procedure indicated in guideline No. (i) only if, having regard to the age, fiscal background and strata of the society to which the claimant belongs and such other considerations, the Tribunal thinks that in the larger interest of the claimant and with a view to ensure the safety of the compensation awarded, it is necessary to invest the amount of compensation in long term fixed deposit. Thus, sufficient discretion has been given to the Tribunal not to insist on investment of the compensation amount in long term fixed deposit and to release even the whole amount in the case of literate persons. It needs to be clarified that the above guidelines were MACT No. 147/2019 Suraj Kumar v. Arvind Kumar Page No. 15/18 BK issued by this Court only to safeguard the interests of the claimants, particularly the minors, illiterates and others whose amounts are sought to be withdrawn on some fictitious grounds.
